clue.text: Fish alone

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flatfish eaten as Dover or lemon variety
second meaning: only, single, without others

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, two unrelated meanings of one four-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a flatfish and also works as an adjective meaning the only one, as in a single heir.

clue.text: University teacher's upset by informer, a member of the Pickwick Club

definitions.text: a member of the Pickwick Club

indicators.note: in a down clue something upset is turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: dons are university teachers; the 's stands for 'is'
grass is British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: A lecturer is distressed after being betrayed by a snitch from a gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: Augustus Snodgrass is one of the club members in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers; 'by' simply places the second piece beside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Snodgrass, the would-be poet, is one of Mr Pickwick's companions in the Dickens novel, so he belongs to that fictional club.

clue.text: Untruths written about young child? That's an understatement

indicators.note: writing something about another thing puts it around it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: untruths are lies
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Fibs told about a toddler are played down as a mild remark.
explanation.walkthrough: LI(TOT)ES. The term is from rhetoric: saying 'not bad' to mean very good.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the figure of speech of ironic understatement, typically affirming something by denying its opposite.

clue.text: Parties can upset a domestic pet

indicators.note: things that are upset are knocked over and scattered, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Loud gatherings can distress a household animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-haired breed of house cat is a typical domestic pet, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: US painter in Cannes, testy

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning the comma

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: An American artist is irritable while on the French Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Estes is an American photorealist painter known for city street scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Estes is a twentieth-century American artist, a leader of the photorealism movement.

clue.text: Team thrills close friends

parts.note: a side is a sports team
kicks are thrills, as in doing it for kicks

explanation.surface: A sports team gets its excitement from its best mates.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidekicks are constant companions or close associates, the loyal partners of a main character.

clue.text: On remand in Taiwan? A girl worried about it

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the last little word
worried in the sense of a dog worrying at something, pulled about until rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman held in custody in Taiwan is anxious about her case.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner on remand is held in custody before their case is heard, i.e. waiting for the court hearing.

clue.text: Check new lease in Cheyne Walk neighbourhood?

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

indicators.note: a new version of a word has its letters made over into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a fresh rental agreement for a flat on a smart London street.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheyne Walk is a historic riverside street in west London; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheyne Walk runs along the Thames in Chelsea, so that London district is the street's neighbourhood.

clue.text: Giant one stolen from Venetian painter

indicators.note: something stolen from a name has been taken out of it, leaving the rest

parts.note: Titian was the great painter of Renaissance Venice
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A huge figure was taken from a work by an Italian old master.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the giant elder gods of Greek myth, and the word now means any person or thing of great size.

clue.text: Drunk, unaware what is happening, is not included

definitions.meaning: second meaning: not following events, dazed
third meaning: left out of something

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of the same short phrase are strung together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being intoxicated, being dazed and oblivious, and being excluded from an activity.

clue.text: Novel, Huckleberry ----? Ask New Age movement

parts.note: Huckleberry Finn is Mark Twain's boy hero

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters are shifted about into another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quiz asks the reader to complete a famous book title, then turns to a New Age trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Age movement' reads as a spiritual trend, but 'New' and 'Age' are fodder and 'movement' scrambles them.
explanation.definitionFit: Finnegans Wake is James Joyce's famously difficult final novel, published in 1939.

clue.text: Local lingo has ring, etc that's peculiar

parts.note: to ring someone is to dial them

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or out of the ordinary, so these letters take an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A regional way of speaking has a strange tone and odd turns of phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is the form of a language spoken in one particular region, its local speech.

clue.text: Hurry up and start cooking some fish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an informal British idiom urging someone to get a move on
second meaning, taken literally: put the skate, a flatfish, on the stove

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a whimsical literal reading: skate is a fish, so putting it on the hob is getting skates on.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting your skates on is a British idiom for hurrying, as if strapping on skates to go faster.

clue.text: Severe wind on face of Eiger

parts.note: Auster is the classical name for the south wind

indicators.note: the face of something is its front, so only the opening letter of the mountain's name is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the Swiss mountain

explanation.surface: A harsh gale blows across the forbidding north face of the Eiger.
explanation.walkthrough: Auster, the Roman south wind, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means stern, harsh or severely plain, a close synonym of severe.

clue.text: Having an enduring popularity, always environmentally friendly

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever
green describes things kind to the environment

explanation.surface: Something stays popular because it has always been eco-conscious.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen song or show stays popular year after year, like a tree that keeps its leaves.

clue.text: Meeting shrink without fear, ultimately

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the word for shrink

parts.note: to contract is to shrink

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter of fear is used

parts.note: the last letter of fear

explanation.surface: An appointment with a psychiatrist leaves the patient finally free of anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' tempts as slang for a psychiatrist, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Contact means a meeting or coming together, as in being in contact with someone.

clue.text: Severely criticise photograph by itself

parts.note: a take is a shot, and to take a picture is to photograph
apart means separately, on its own

explanation.surface: Someone harshly attacks a picture shown on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To take apart an argument or a performer is to demolish them with harsh criticism, an idiom.

clue.text: Talked about an American city

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for talked surrounds the little word

parts.note: spoke is the past tense of speak
taken as written

explanation.surface: People discussed a town in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Spokane is a city in eastern Washington state in the USA.

clue.text: Speech about keeping correspondence

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one word is enclosed by the other

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
a ratio is a correspondence between quantities

explanation.surface: A talk on the subject of letters that someone holds on to.
explanation.walkthrough: O(RATIO)N: 'correspondence' suggests letters, but it is the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal speech, delivered on a ceremonial occasion.

clue.text: Check group to the rear

parts.note: a set is a group
back means at the rear

explanation.surface: Someone inspects the people standing at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a check to progress, a reverse or hindrance that halts advance.

clue.text: A new Italian poet gets musical instruction

parts.note: taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new
Dante Alighieri, author of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A fresh Italian writer of verse is given a music lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a tempo marking on a score telling players to perform at a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: A father's involved tale about new edition of novel

indicators.note: about means around, so the story word wraps round the rearranged letters

parts.note: taken as written
pa is a familiar word for father, with the possessive s
a saga is a long tale

indicators.note: a new version of the following word has its letters made over

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dad is caught up in a story about the latest edition of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' only joins the pieces; the story word is split open to hold the rearranged edition. Forster's novel ends the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Passage to India is E. M. Forster's 1924 novel about British rule in India.

clue.text: Fear a thrash must include leader of radicals

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of radicals

explanation.surface: A dread that a beating must involve a militant ringleader.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear or anxious apprehension of danger.

clue.text: Reportedly followed pamphlet

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken or heard, so the word sounds right but is spelt differently

parts.note: to follow a trail is to track it

explanation.surface: A leaflet, so people say, came next.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political, written to persuade.

clue.text: Upset a philanthropist hiding soldier

indicators.note: hiding something means keeping it tucked inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written
Henry Tate, sugar magnate who funded the Tate gallery
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A wealthy benefactor sheltering a serviceman causes distress.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Tate, the sugar refiner, founded London's Tate gallery; the soldier slips between 'a' and his name.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate someone is to disturb or trouble them, making them upset.

clue.text: A volunteer force around LA, extremely neat US city

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the volunteer force encloses what follows

parts.note: taken as written
the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve army
taken as written

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so only its outer letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters of neat

explanation.surface: Reservists surround Los Angeles in a very tidy operation in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the capital city of the US state of Georgia.

clue.text: Mischievous children pinching loaf and goober peas

indicators.note: pinching means gripping between, so one word nips the other inside

parts.note: naughty children are cheeky monkeys
loaf and nut are both slang for the head; loaf from rhyming slang loaf of bread

explanation.surface: Naughty kids steal bread and peanuts.
explanation.walkthrough: MONKEY(NUT)S. 'Loaf' looks like bread but is the head, from Cockney rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Goober peas is American Southern slang for peanuts, which in Britain are monkey nuts in their shells.

clue.text: Check tax

definitions.meaning: first meaning: examine or try out
second meaning: strain or make demands on, as in taxing patience

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax' looks like a levy, but it is the verb meaning to strain.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something is to examine it, and also to stretch it, as a trial tests one's endurance.
